Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-03 15:30 UTC | Duration: 39 minutes | Location: Zoom | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Linda Gomez (Cygnus CISO), Alan Price (Cygnus Sec Eng), Rashid Khan (Cygnus Compliance), Priya Shah (Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through what admin/audit logs capture, export options (S3, webhook, SIEM), retention defaults and enterprise options, and encryption/KMS integration. Cygnus asked about retention, per-tenant segregation, and whether model prompt contents are included in admin logs; next steps agreed to share SOC2 and sample exports and a follow-up SIEM integration deep-dive.

Topics: audit logs, admin activity, export formats, retention, KMS, RBAC/SSO access to logs, SIEM integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick introductions? I'll hand it to Linda to start on the Cygnus side.
[00:07] Linda: Hi, Linda Gomez, CISO at Cygnus Finance... Alan Price, security eng, Rashid compliance, and Priya on platform. we wanted to focus today mainly on audit logs and admin activity, what you capture, export options and retention.
[00:20] Maya: great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Ethan will run through the technical bits and I'll add policy/contract-level notes.
[00:26] Ethan: thanks. quick agenda: what events we capture, separation of admin vs data plane, export and streaming options, encryption/KMS, retention and immutability options, and RBAC access control for log viewing. sound good?
[00:36] Alan: yes. and we, uh, we also want to confirm whether prompt or model inputs are part of these logs or not - that's a big ask for our compliance folks.
[00:45] Ethan: totally. short answer: admin activity logs do not capture full model prompt content by default. they capture metadata about API calls (timestamp, caller identity, endpoint, response codes, model id, request size), and admin/config changes - user provisioning, role changes, key rotation, model upload/versioning, deploy actions. we do have separate audit trails for inference requests if you enable request logging, but that's treated as data plane logs and subject to different retention and export controls.
[01:10] Rashid: can you say more about the separate trails? like, are inference request logs stored in the same bucket?
[01:16] Ethan: good question. by default platform separates control-plane/admin events from data-plane request logs at the storage level. for enterprise customers we can push both to the same S3 prefix if you want, or keep them isolated. we support S3 export, push to cloud logging (e.g., BigQuery), and webhook/syslog/Kafka forwarding to your SIEM.
[01:33] Priya: when you say "push" is that near real-time? or batched?
[01:36] Ethan: we support streaming webhooks for near-real-time, and daily/ hourly batch exports to S3. streaming is best-effort low latency, batch is for retention/archival. the streaming webhook retries with exponential backoff, and we provide a dead-letter queue when deliveries fail.
[01:52] Linda: about retention - what is the default? and can we extend to, say, 2 years?
[01:57] Ethan: default for control-plane/admin logs is 90 days on hosted plans. for enterprise we offer configurable retention up to multiple years; typical patterns are 1-7 years depending on regs. we also support export to your S3 for indefinite retention and write-once stores for immutability if you need e-discovery.
[02:14] Maya: and to add, retention in console is configurable via policy and can be locked with a legal hold feature for investigations. we'll need to surface that in the contract if you require retention periods or deletion waivers.
[02:26] Alan: encryption - at-rest and in-transit? key management?
[02:29] Ethan: all logs are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest using AES-256. for hosted we use customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for enterprise plans - you can bring your own CMK which we use to envelope-encrypt logs before writing to object storage. for HSM-backed keys we have an option via our Private deployment.
[02:48] Rashid: how does key rotation work for exported logs? if we rotate the KMS key, will older objects still be readable?
[02:54] Ethan: yes, envelope encryption means objects are encrypted with a data key that's itself encrypted with your CMK. key rotation in KMS keeps older ciphertexts decryptable; we can also re-encrypt archives on request.
[03:03] Priya: what about access controls for who can see logs inside Redwood console?
[03:06] Ethan: RBAC covers log access. roles like Admin, ReadOnly-Security, Auditor -- you can create custom roles. only users with the log-audit view permission can see full event details. access is recorded as well - so viewing the logs generates an admin event.
[03:20] Linda: good. what about API keys? do audit logs capture API key creation and usage?
[03:24] Ethan: yes - key creation, rotation, revocation, and failed auth attempts are logged. usage metrics (which key used, IP, region) are in data-plane logs if enabled.
[03:31] Alan: SIEM integration - we use Splunk and Datadog for different teams. what's the recommended approach?
[03:35] Ethan: two common patterns: 1) push daily/ hourly batches to a customer S3, then your SIEM ingests from S3; 2) streaming syslog/webhook to SIEM for near-real-time alerts. we provide JSONL schema and a Splunk HEC example. for Datadog we have a direct ingestion example and tag mapping. we'll share example parsers.
[03:54] Maya: note: if you want to maintain parity with existing internal schemas, we can provide a mapping sheet and lightweight lambda to transform the JSON to your fields.
[04:02] Rashid: are there any PII concerns in the admin logs? i.e. do usernames or email addresses appear?
[04:07] Ethan: user identifiers are logged (user id, email hash depending on config). we do not include request bodies or prompt text by default. if you enable request logging for inference we can mask or redact sensitive fields before export - there are configurable redaction rules and a transform pipeline before export.
[04:25] Linda: retention across regions - we have EU residency requirements for some lines of business; can logs be stored in a specific region?
[04:31] Ethan: yes - region pinning for exports is supported. for hosted we can route log writes to S3 buckets in your specified region or run the private control plane in a VPC region. for strict residency we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with network controls.
[04:46] Alan: is there any risk of cross-tenant access? how do you logically segregate logs?
[04:50] Ethan: logs are labeled with tenant id and isolated at storage layer; multi-tenant metadata separation + IAM policies prevent cross-tenant reads. for dedicated/private customers we can provide physical separation with dedicated buckets or accounts.
[05:02] Priya: about schema - what's included in an admin event record?
[05:05] Ethan: typical fields: event_id, timestamp, actor {id, email, role}, action_type (user.create, role.assign, api_key.create, model.deploy), target_resource (resource_type, id), ip_address, user_agent, request_id, outcome (success/failure), and a free-form detail field with small text descriptions. For large payloads we reference an object in object storage rather than inline.
[05:31] Linda: can you show a sample record?
[05:33] Ethan: sure, we'll send a sample JSONL record after the call - it'll include the schema and an example with masked user info.
[05:39] Maya: couple policy clarifications: SOC 2 - we have a SOC 2 Type II report and can provide it under an NDA. ISO status is in progress; we expect cert to be completed Q1 2027.
[05:51] Rashid: do you provide audit logs for admin actions performed by Redwood staff on our tenant?
[05:56] Ethan: yes, actions performed by Redwood operators on customer environments are logged and available to you; operator access is controlled and audited.
[06:04] Alan: how long do you keep operator access logs? same as customer admin logs?
[06:08] Ethan: yes by default same retention, but we can mirror operator logs to separate immutable storage for longer retention if required.
[06:18] Priya: how about exports - are they gzipped? what formats?
[06:21] Ethan: we support compressed JSONL (gzip), newline-delimited JSON, Parquet for analytical workloads, and CSV for simple fields. S3 exports are zipped by default and have a manifest.
[06:32] Linda: compliance question - can we get cryptographic proof of log integrity?
[06:36] Ethan: we support write-once buckets and an append-only log with SHA256 checksums for each file. we can provide manifests signed by our KMS key and can integrate with your verification process.
[06:48] Maya: one nuance - the control plane will not retain full plaintext inference data unless you enable request logging; we make that explicit in the security docs.
[06:57] Rashid: ok so if we enable request logging for a pilot, we need to sign off on retention and encryption for that dataset?
[07:02] Ethan: correct. enabling request logging is an opt-in and has its own retention and export controls; we can add redaction rules for PII before export.
[07:12] Alan: are there built-in alerts for suspicious admin activity?
[07:15] Ethan: yes we have anomaly detection for admin events (e.g., mass role grants, abnormal IP geolocation), and you can push those detections to your SIEM or use our alerting rules to notify Slack/PagerDuty.
[07:27] Maya: note: we'll include example detection rules and a sample playbook on escalation.
[07:32] Linda: last contract question: if we require data residency and a contractual clause for log retention, is that something you accommodate?
[07:38] Maya: yes that's standard for enterprise engagements; we have addenda for residency and retention, and legal hold wording. will include in the packet.
[07:46] Priya: small ops question - who in Redwood will we contact for export failures?
[07:50] Sofia: CSM triage first (that's me), then Ethan as SE for troubleshooting, and MA within support for escalations; we'll provide an on-call rotation for enterprise.
[07:59] Alan: any rate limits on log exports or streaming?
[08:02] Ethan: for streaming webhooks we throttle per account to protect delivery; for enterprise we can increase rate limits and provide dedicated egress. batch exports have no practical limit but we chunk files to sizes that are friendly for SIEM ingestion.
[08:15] Rashid: question on deletion: if we delete a user, are their events removed?
[08:19] Ethan: deletion requests do not retroactively remove historical audit events by default. you can request redaction which will replace PII fields with a hash or remove entries subject to policy and legal constraints. full deletion is possible for customers who require it, but we document it as a special request and may need to adjust retention manifests.
[08:37] Linda: ok thanks. can you reiterate the deliverables?
[08:40] Maya: yes - SOC2 report and encryption doc from me by 2026-12-07; Ethan will send sample exports and SIEM examples by 2026-12-10; schedule follow-up for SIEM deep-dive week of 12/14 once you're confirmed retention.
[08:54] Alan: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:56] Ethan: thanks, we'll follow up in writing and attach the JSONL schema and Splunk HEC example.
[09:02] Linda: thanks, bye.
